question: How deep must each possible nearby star eclipse, as a function of unknown aperture throughput, to supply the observed SAP dip? Conditional brightness feasibility, not host inference or probability.
method: Already-opened native SAP only. Four SPOC sectors each; unchanged clocks from preceding shape/baseline plans. Quality-zero finite-positive SAP/error/time. Normalize by sector median. Each event within +/-3D requires >=2 transit samples and >=5 outside samples on each side. Joint shared exposure-integrated box + per-event linear intercept/slope. Median native cadence approximates exposure. Error covariance scaled by max(1,chi2/dof); divide decrement by mean fitted event intercept, propagate full covariance. No new data, period fit, event selection or cutout model.
neighbor_policy: Every cached TIC row within 150 arcsec including target; preserve missing Tmag and duplicate/ambiguous entries; each row an alternative, never sum catalog flux. Use catalog T-band ratios only, not Gaia G as T. No new Gaia queries or image flux.
formula: r=10**(-0.4*(T_neighbor-T_target)); c=CROWDSAP model target aperture fraction; eta=FLFRCSAP model target throughput; q=neighbor throughput / target throughput; e=d_SAP/(c*r*q). q physically <=1/eta conditional on header model. Compute q_min=d/(c*r) for e<=1 and optimistic minimum e=d*eta/(c*r). Feasibility additionally requires c*r*q<=1-c for a neighbor; target has r=q=1. No claimed physical clearance from conditional bounds.
sensitivity: q values0.25,0.5,1,1/eta; formal +/-3sigma depth; +/-3 catalog sigma delta-mag using hypot; missing magnitude errors retained unknown, not zero for clearance. Header c and eta each +/-10percent relative clipped0.001..1 as arbitrary sensitivity not confidence interval. Brightest-neighbor magnitude, shallowest depth, lowest eta, highest c yield optimistic bound. No statistical calibration or exclusions.
verification: Independent algebra using direct synthetic flux loss and inverse equations, exact raw/hash identity, normal equations, reconstruct fit masks/design and coefficients independently; preserve all sector/source/assumption alternatives.
